Wednesday 6 January 2027 P1, 40 minutes, Year A, group three to four, Level 2 aids on every task, 10–15-minute chunks, no public questions or personal disclosure, private generic help route. Next GROW PSHE Week 1 after Downloaded.

source_end_check: Recognise in a fictional example that a changed plan can feel hard.
timing: 3 calm start and starter; 4 input; 4 model; 1 reset.
6 guided story; 3 private hinge; 3 help choice; 1 reset.
source_timing: No fixed lesson minutes in row 64; owner specifies 40 minutes and 10–15-minute chunks.

routes.Supported: Read one short line at a time. Keep word bank, starter and visible model. Offer two choices, pointing, an aid or a faithful scribe. Use the same change-and-feeling goal. Record any answer cue.
routes.Independent: Use story D with the word bank, starter and visible model still in view. Identify the change and link it to the stated feeling. Choose a helpful step. Normal reading or scribing access stays available.
routes.Aspire: Keep all Level 2 aids. Explain why the new plan could feel hard, then use story C to show that two people can feel differently. More writing or personal disclosure is not required.

level_2_scaffolds_every_task.model: Old plan: art first. Model: “Art is first.”
Story A: “The time changed. They feel cross.”
Story A: “The time changed. They feel cross.”
Story A: one person feels cross. That is one person’s feeling.
Story A: “They could ask an adult to show the plan.”
Story A: “The time changed. They feel cross.”

level_2_scaffolds_every_task.starter: Change can feel ... . A kind step is ... .
level_2_scaffolds_every_task.model: Story A: “Change can feel hard. An adult can show the plan.”

colour_blind_safe: Words, numbered cards and clear black text carry all meaning. No colour-only answer codes.

cases.title: A new time
cases.text: A young person will do art later today. The old plan was art first. They say, “I feel cross. I liked the old plan.”
cases.clue: I feel cross. I liked the old plan.
cases.help: An adult can show the new plan.

cases.title: A new room
cases.text: The room for a group task is shut today. The group will use a new room. A young person says, “I feel unsure. I do not know where to sit.”
cases.change: The group will use a new room.
cases.clue: I feel unsure. I do not know where to sit.
cases.help: An adult can show where to sit.

cases.title: A new pair
cases.text: Two young people will each work with a new partner. One says, “I feel keen to start.” The other says, “I feel unsure.”
cases.change: Each will work with a new partner.
cases.clue: I feel keen to start. I feel unsure.
cases.help: An adult can explain the first step.

cases.title: A new order
cases.text: A group used to draw first, then read. Today the group will read first, then draw. A young person says, “I feel cross. I liked the old order.”
cases.change: Read is first and draw is later.
cases.clue: I feel cross. I liked the old order.
cases.help: An adult can show the first step.

private_help_route: Say: “You can ask a trusted adult in private. You can point to HELP or say ‘Can we talk in private?’ You do not have to tell the group.” Use the school’s help route. If the first adult is busy or help is not enough, use the route to another trusted adult. A learner may pass, pause or use a neutral task and return with support.
scribed_route: Read the story without adding a feeling. Let the learner point, sign, use an aid or speak. Write the exact selection or words, read them back quietly and allow correction. Record reader/scribe access separately from an adult-supplied answer. No public retelling is needed.
worked_example_and_fade: Read A. Point to “art later” and “old plan was art first”. Say: “The time changed. The young person says they feel cross. The old plan felt familiar. Change can feel hard.” Show the written model. For B, ask privately for the changed thing, then for the feeling clue. Reduce answer cues only; leave the model, bank and frame visible.
prompt_ladder: 1 Point to place or instruction. 2 Ask one short question privately. 3 Rephrase instruction. 4 Offer scaffold or choice. 5 Model the first step only, then return the task. Allow processing time between prompts. In input, point to the words; in guided work, elicit one clue; in individual work, log help and fade answer prompts.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: one line at a time, visible example and short tasks. Communication and Interaction: literal words, wait time, aid and exact scribe. SEMH: predictable plan, private responses, pass and supported pause. Sensory and Physical: clear text, uncluttered page, comfortable seat and usual aids. EAL: read with the learner, point to the same words, rehearse privately and plan in any language. Numbers and words carry meaning; colour is optional.
misconceptions: “All change is bad.” Correct: a change can feel hard, welcome or mixed. “Everyone must feel the same.” Correct: use C’s two different feelings. “A hard feeling means failure.” Correct: it can happen; support and time may help. Never grade the feeling itself.
success: Identify a change in a fictional story.
Link the changed plan to the stated hard feeling.
Recognise that change can feel hard.

evidence.description: Dated individual change-and-feeling response to D, or supported B, with access, answer prompts, first response, one next step and reply. Helpful step extends the exact recognition outcome.

assessment: Secure: identifies a change and recognises its link to a hard feeling in the fictional example. Partial: identifies the change or feeling but not the link. Not yet: requires further modelling. Unobserved: no response collected, including a pass. Record actual access and answer prompts, not an assumed independent response.
where_this_leads: This helps me cope with a changed plan and ask for clear steps in learning or future work.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Wednesday 6 January 2027 · P1 · 40 minutes · Year A
BUILD · three to four learners · Spring 1 Week 1 · formative
Theme: Resilience & Change. Spring 1 has six weeks. Week 6 is assessing.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
Recognise that change can feel hard (Children's MH Week).
Source: BUILD Weekly - Spring, row 64, PSHE & Citizenship. B64 Spr1·W1; C64 exact outcome. Source strand and resource names are rendered generically under the names rule.

A change to a familiar plan can feel hard. People can have different feelings about the same change. The lesson recognises feelings without judging them or diagnosing a problem. It does not require a personal story.
Success: identify what changes in a fictional story; link the change to the stated feeling; recognise that change can feel hard. A helpful step extends this learning.

Books, pens, four copies of Support Cards and Vocabulary Mat, plus the adult evidence record. No scissors, phone, login or internet needed. Check the actual private help route and a place for a supported pause before teaching. Give an arrival task straight away. Arrange quiet individual response turns, not public questions.

The parenthetical Children’s MH Week label is retained verbatim from C64. It is a curriculum label, not a claim that the event occurs on 6 January. The owner supplies this date and P1. Source D64–F64 names are replaced with generic feelings work, fictional scenarios and an evidence record; no accreditation is claimed.
This helps me cope with a changed plan and ask for clear steps in learning or future work.
3 calm start and starter; 4 input; 4 model; 1 reset.
6 guided story; 3 private hinge; 3 help choice; 1 reset.

The chunks last 12, 13 and 15 minutes. Two one-minute resets are already included in the 40 minutes. Give extra access time by reducing repetitions, never by requiring disclosure. Slides 11 and 12 add no teaching time.

0–3: settle and privately compare “art first” with “art later”. Teach the link between a fictional changed plan and a stated hard feeling. Do not ask about personal experience, family change or health. The source’s MH Week label is not an event-date claim. Generic scenario work replaces named resources; no therapeutic or accreditation claim is made.

New plan: art later. Old plan model: art first. A changes the time/order of art. Cross is stated, not inferred from a face. A person’s feeling can be acknowledged without judging it. The model makes the link explicit.

The room changes. Unsure is stated; the learner does not know where to sit. A useful link is “The room is new. They feel unsure because they do not know where to sit.” Asking an adult to show the seat fits the uncertainty. The adult must not assume how every person would feel.

Main key B: the two people feel differently, keen and unsure. Both responses are possible. Parallel key A: change may feel hard, supported by cross in A. Use the bank, starter and model throughout. If the learner chooses the other answer, point to the quotes, re-model and check privately. No public hands-up check.

For B, choice A asking where to sit fits the story. For the general step, choice A asking for a first step fits. Guessing may leave the uncertainty unresolved. Help may clarify the plan without making the feeling disappear. Accept an equivalent safe step such as asking to see the plan or taking an agreed pause with support.

“The order changed. They will read first, then draw. They feel cross because they liked the old order. Change can feel hard. They could ask an adult to show the first step.” A short equivalent, pointing to the correct clue with a scribe, or an aided reply can show the same thinking.

Secure recognition links the change with its stated hard feeling. A help step extends learning. Do not require a coping performance or a claim that the feeling is gone. Naming cross without linking it to change is partial. A pass or no collected response is unobserved, not failure.

Give one precise next step: show what changed; find the feeling clue; link the two. Use the frame and visible model for the reply. Keep first thinking and revision separate. Record usual access separately from content cues. All routes retain Level 2 supports.

Review/exit: hard/cross/unsure/ask/help, change-and-kind-step frame and A model.

Read neutrally, wait, capture exact selections, read back and allow correction. No public response is required. Help request can be a private point to HELP. “Change is always bad”: use C’s keen response. “All people feel the same”: use the two quotes in C. “Hard feelings mean failure”: acknowledge the feeling and offer a clear next step. “Help must fix it at once”: support can help while feelings take time. Accept mixed feelings when the learner explains a possibility, while distinguishing what the story actually says.

Supported: reduce reading at one time, offer choices and record help. Independent: learner chooses the link using retained aids. Aspire: give a reason and compare C’s responses. No route adds personal disclosure. Shorter writing, pointing or exact scribing preserves the same outcome.
